tickets.title: Secure Password Hashing (Bcrypt)
tickets.description: Upgrade a legacy application that stores passwords in plaintext to use `bcrypt` hashing with a secure work factor.
tasks: Upgrade a legacy application that stores passwords in plaintext to use `bcrypt` hashing with a secure work factor.
common_mistakes: Storing the salt separately in another database column (bcrypt includes the salt in the output hash string)
Using MD5 or SHA256 without a salt.
hints: Remember to encode your strings to bytes before hashing them.

solution.auth.py:
import bcrypt

    def hash_password(plain_text_password):
        # Convert password to bytes
        password_bytes = plain_text_password.encode('utf-8')
        
        # Generate salt and hash (work factor / rounds is 12 by default)
        salt = bcrypt.gensalt()
        hashed = bcrypt.hashpw(password_bytes, salt)
        
        return hashed.decode('utf-8') # Store this string in the DB

    def verify_password(plain_text_password, hashed_password):
        # Check if the provided password matches the stored hash
        password_bytes = plain_text_password.encode('utf-8')
        hash_bytes = hashed_password.encode('utf-8')
        
        return bcrypt.checkpw(password_bytes, hash_bytes)

tickets.title: JWT Verification & Signature Checking
tickets.description: Write a middleware function to parse a JSON Web Token (JWT) from the `Authorization` header and verify its signature using an HS256 secret key.
tasks: Write a middleware function to parse a JSON Web Token (JWT) from the `Authorization` header and verify its signature using an HS256 secret key.
tickets.evaluation: Sandbox execution sends expired tokens and tokens signed with invalid keys to ensure the middleware rejects them with a 401.
common_mistakes: Trusting the payload data without verifying the signature
hints: Ensure you explicitly pass the `algorithms=["HS256"]` parameter to prevent algorithm confusion attacks.
